# [FEATURE] Systemd Journal Log Priority Mapping

## Problem Statement
When running pghoard as a systemd service, all log messages are captured with the same default priority level (typically INFO), regardless of their actual severity. This makes it impossible to distinguish between critical error messages and routine informational messages in the systemd journal.

## Missing Capability
The application lacks the ability to properly map Python logging levels to systemd journal priorities when running as a service. Without this capability, log severity information is lost during capture by systemd.

System administrators and monitoring tools need to filter and alert on error-level logs while ignoring informational messages. Tools like journalpump rely on proper priority mapping to selectively process and forward only error logs to alerting systems or log aggregation platforms.

## Current Limitation
Currently, pghoard logs to stderr/stdout which systemd captures with a uniform priority level. This means that critical errors appear with the same priority as routine informational messages, preventing effective log filtering and monitoring based on severity.

"},"workdir":{"type":"string","description":"The working directory to execute the command in. Defaults to the current directory.
"},"timeout_ms":{"type":"integer","description":"Timeout for the command in milliseconds. None means no timeout.
"},"mode":{"type":"string","description":"Optional. Either "shell" (default) or "shell_command". Plain strings run through the user's shell with `-lc`; this field is kept only for Codex compatibility and can usually be omitted.
"},"description":{"type":"string","description":"Brief description of what the command does.
"}}

function.name: apply_patch
function.description: Apply a patch to create, update, or delete files using Codex's patch format. The patch format supports "Add File", "Update File" (with diff hunks), "Delete File", and "Move to" operations. Update hunks must match the old file contents exactly; insertion-only hunks without context fail. Python files are syntax-checked after modification, and the patch is rolled back if an error occurs.

parameters.properties:
{"patch":{"type":"string","description":"The full patch text in Codex patch format. Example:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: path/to/file.py
@@ context hint
 context line
-old line
+new line
*** End Patch
"},"cwd":{"type":"string","description":"Working directory for resolving relative paths in the patch. Defaults to the current directory.
"}}

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read the contents of a file from the local filesystem. Supports reading specific line ranges via offset and limit parameters. Output is prefixed with line numbers; empty files print `File is empty.`.

parameters.properties:
{"file_path":{"type":"string","description":"The absolute or relative path of the file to read.
"},"offset":{"type":"integer","description":"The 1-indexed line number to start reading from. Negative values count backwards from the end (e.g. -1 is the last line).
"},"limit":{"type":"integer","description":"The maximum number of lines to read.
"}}

function.name: rg
function.description: Search file contents using regex patterns via ripgrep (rg). Prefers the external rg binary when available, falls back to a pure-Python regex search otherwise.

parameters.properties:
{"pattern":{"type":"string","description":"The regex pattern to search for in file contents.
"},"path":{"type":"string","description":"File or directory to search in. Defaults to the current working directory.
"},"glob":{"type":"string","description":"Glob pattern to filter which files to search (e.g. "*.py", "*.{ts,tsx}").
"},"ignore_case":{"type":"boolean","description":"Case insensitive search. Default: false.
"},"max_count":{"type":"integer","description":"Maximum number of matching lines per file to return.
"}}

function.name: delete
function.description: Delete a file at the specified path. The tool reports an error if the file does not exist, is not a regular file, or permission is denied.

parameters.properties: {"file_path":{"type":"string","description":"The absolute or relative path of the file to delete.\n"}}

function.name: update_plan
function.description: Update the task plan with a structured list of steps and their statuses. Each step has a status of "pending", "in_progress", or "completed". At most one step can be in_progress at a time.

parameters.properties: {"plan":{"type":"string","description":"A JSON array of plan items, each with \"step\" (string) and \"status\" (one of \"pending\", \"in_progress\", \"completed\").\n"},"explanation":{"type":"string","description":"Optional explanation of the plan update.\n"}}
